query: How do replication slots determine which WAL segments must be retained and prevent them from being removed?

matches.reason: Scans all replication slots to compute the minimum restart_lsn (the oldest WAL location any slot still needs) and publishes it to the xlog subsystem.
Shared-memory accessors that store/retrieve the slot-required minimum LSN, bridging the slot subsystem's computation to WAL segment retention decisions.

Core enforcement logic: retreats the WAL segment eligible for removal to no later than what replication slots require (plus max_slot_wal_keep_size/wal_keep_size limits), preventing needed segments from being deleted.
